metadata.title: Who Can Approve?
metadata.note: Weekly update (changelog framing). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. One ticket: split the reviewer and viewer dashboards. The reviewer panel (approve) was bolted onto the public search page, so anyone browsing could approve. Fix: new frontend/review.html (366 lines) — per-dimension confidence chips by level, evidence counts, anomalies, full brief, inline brief editor, notes, approve; offline fallback to sample data. frontend/index.html — reviewer panel extracted, 1,131 → 983 lines, now a clean viewer that links to the review page. Silent bug fixed in passing: the old textarea was labelled 'Reviewer notes / corrected brief' but code only sent `notes`, so corrections were silently filed as notes and the API's corrected-brief capability was unreachable; new page separates the fields and sends `brief` only when it changed. Bookends render; body B01-B03 are house-style 4K PIL cards (make_cards.py). DOUBLE-CHECK LAW: figures from the creator's change log.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. One ticket this week, but a sharp one. The reviewer controls, approving a brief, were sitting right on the public search page. So anyone just browsing could also approve. And while I was in there, I found corrections quietly vanishing. Let's split the dashboards, and fix that.

props.command: Why could anyone browsing briefs also approve them — and where did the corrections go?
output: approve was on the public page

beats.narration_text: Here's the setup. The reviewer panel was bolted onto the page everyone uses to browse briefs. There was no line between looking at a brief and approving one, same page, same buttons. But approving is a privilege, not a view. Having it one click away for every visitor is the kind of thing that's fine until it very much isn't.

show.event: the four problem cards snap in

card.title: Everyone Could Approve.
card.subtitle: no line between view and act

items.quote: reviewer controls on the public page
a browser could approve a brief
approval is a privilege, not a view

card.caption: the reviewer panel was bolted onto the page everyone uses to browse

beats.narration_text: So I split it in two. The public page, index dot html, is now a clean viewer, just browse, with a link through to the review page. All the reviewer machinery moved out: that's eleven-thirty-one lines down to nine-eighty-three. And a new page, review dot html, is the dedicated reviewer dashboard, confidence chips by dimension, evidence counts, anomalies, the full brief, an inline editor, notes, and approve. It even falls back to sample data with an offline banner if the API is down.

card.title: Two Pages Now.
card.subtitle: viewer, and reviewer
card.caption: the reviewer machinery moved to its own page — chips, evidence, anomalies, inline editor, approve
card.footer: VIEWER PAGE · REVIEWER PAGE · A LINK BETWEEN

beats.narration_text: Now the bug I found in passing. The old reviewer box was labelled notes, slash, corrected brief. But the code only ever sent the notes field. So if you carefully rewrote a brief, your correction was silently filed as a note, and the API's whole corrected-brief feature was unreachable, nobody could actually use it. The new page separates the two fields, and sends the brief only when it actually changed.

show.at: only ever sent the notes field

card.title: The Silent Correction.
card.subtitle: a field that went nowhere
card.caption: a textarea promised 'corrected brief' but the code never sent it — real edits vanished
card.footer: A LABEL THE CODE DIDN'T HONOUR = LOST WORK

beats.narration_text: The theme: separate what people can do, not just what they see, approval belongs on its own page. And watch for inputs that go nowhere, a field labelled one thing but sent as another loses real work without a single error.

artifactLines: The reviewer panel sat on the public search page — anyone browsing could approve a brief.
Split in two: index.html is now a clean viewer (1,131 → 983 lines) linking to a new review.html (366 lines).
The reviewer page: per-dimension confidence chips, evidence counts, anomalies, inline brief editor, notes, approve.
Silent bug: a 'corrected brief' textarea only ever sent notes — corrections vanished. Now the fields are separate.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Look at one tool you've built. Can someone who should only view also act, delete, approve, edit, because the controls share a page? And check one form: does every field you ask for actually get sent, and used? A label that promises more than the code delivers is a quiet way to lose people's work.

props.command: In one tool I built: can a view-only user also act (approve / delete / edit) because the controls share a page? And does every field in one of my forms actually get sent and used?
output: separate what people can DO, not just see
a privilege doesn't belong on the public page
a field that isn't sent loses real work

beats.narration_text: Who can approve. Separate the powers. Humanitarians AI.
